note:
Job Samuel W Palethorpe, engraver, a widower of 60 with his daughter and two servants at **10 Pelham Terrace** on the 1891 return - the house now numbered **29 Newcastle Drive** (#222). Transcribed from the census image by Claude at A. Hagues's request. 29 Newcastle Drive held only 1921, so 1891 is free, and none of the four was in the record.

**The placement is by the conversion rule**, 39 minus the Pelham Terrace number, fixed by two confirmed pairs - 12 to 27 (Glendower, the Fosters) and 24 to 15. 39 - 10 = 29.

**A directory line that looks like a contradiction but is not.** Wright's Directory 1898-99 prints 'Mr. Job S. Palethorpe' at '10 Pelham **Crescent**'. That volume runs an even-numbered Pelham Crescent section which is really a stretch of Pelham Terrace - the same section that gives Glendower at 12, the Foster house now proved to be 27 Newcastle Drive. The crescent's genuine even side is a different pair of houses of about 1870-75 by Barrack Lane, occupied by the Mellers and Levis in 1911. So the 1898-99 line is this same man at this same house, seven years on, under a mistaken heading, and it supports the number 10 rather than undermining it.

His occupation has a second word after 'Engraver' which is struck through on the schedule and which I cannot read; only Engraver is recorded. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 10 Pelham Terrace (now 29 Newcastle Drive), read from the census image supplied by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1898-99, page 109 (Leicester Special Collections id 165285).
